subject: Enclave forwarder handshake — Splunk HEC ingestion for Redwood Private
messages:
From: Aaron Bell <aaron.bell@acmehealth.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acmehealth.com>, Jing Wu <jing.wu@security-ops.com>

Subject: Splunk HEC from enclave forwarder — onboarding request

Hi Chloe,

We're in the final stages of onboarding Redwood Private for production telemetry. Security wants a concrete plan for getting logs and traces from our VPC enclave into our Splunk instance via an internal forwarder. Constraints:

- No direct outbound to public Splunk endpoints (must go through Redwoods-prescribed proxy or private link).
- mTLS preferred for HEC; we need certificate rotation guidance and CSR process.
- Retention and chain-of-custody requirements for SOC 2 audit (we need evidence we can prove delivery or safe fallback).
- Trace correlation: we run OpenTelemetry; spans should include the Redwood request id when possible.

Attached is a short spec of our current HEC settings and a sample event (acme_hec_requirements.pdf, acme-forwarder-sample-event.json). Can you confirm the recommended topology (enclave forwarder -> internal egress proxy -> Splunk HEC collector), firewall ports, and the minimal configuration the forwarder needs? Also: what failure modes do you recommend (local buffering, S3 archive fallback, canary checks)?

Thanks — if useful we can set a 30-minute working session next week.

Best,
Aaron Bell
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Splunk HEC from enclave forwarder — onboarding request

Hi Aaron — thanks for the spec and sample. Looping in Rishi (infra/integration) and Naomi (security/compliance) to lock down the plan. High level proposal:

1) Topology we recommend
- Enclave-forwarder (containerized collector inside customer VPC) -> Redwood private egress proxy (customer-managed ENI or PrivateLink) -> Splunk HEC collector (on-prem or private IP).
- For air-gapped pockets we support a forwarder that writes compressed batches locally and ships to an S3 staging bucket over a VPC endpoint during maintenance windows.

2) Security and certs
- We support mTLS for HEC. Redwood can accept a client cert from your PKI; we can also generate a CSR for you to sign. Cert rotation: our suggested cadence is 90 days with automated renewal via a signed CSR exchange.

3) Observability/trace hooks
- Forwarder will add a redwood_request_id header to synced events where available; OTLP sidecar can export spans to Redwood tracing gateway (OTLP/gRPC). We will map span.trace_id -> Splunk field "trace_id" for cross-linking.

4) Failure modes and evidence
- Primary: realtime POST to HEC; retries with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Secondary: durable local queue with size limits (configurable) and periodic ship to S3 over a VPC endpoint (immutable archive bundle).
- Evidence: every bundle includes manifest.json (batch id, sha256 of files, start/end timestamps) so you can present chain-of-custody during audits.

Action items for us to proceed:
- (Aaron) Share a test HEC endpoint (IP/hostname), port, HEC token, and preferred auth mode (token vs mTLS).
- (Rishi) we'll prepare a forwarder image and checklist.
- (Naomi) will propose the audit artifact template we use for SOC 2 evidence.

I'll attach our onboarding checklist and a skeleton forwarder config. If that looks good we'll schedule a 1hr hands-on session.

-Chloe
Product Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Aaron/Chloe — quick technical notes and a sample config snippet. We'll formalize this into a short runbook during the hands-on.

1) Network/firewall
- Required outbound: tcp/8088 (HEC) from the egress proxy to your Splunk collector IP. If you use HEC over TLS on a different port please provide it.
- If using PrivateLink/Private Endpoint: allow the specific ENI private IPs; no NAT required.

2) HEC and mTLS
- If you choose mTLS: forwarder presents cert, Splunk validates. We'll provide a CSR generator if you need; otherwise share the PEM and we pre-load into the forwarder image.

3) Forwarder config (high level)
- batching:
  max_batch_size: 5000
  flush_interval_ms: 3000
  gzip: true
- retry:
  max_retries: 8
  backoff_base_ms: 250
  backoff_max_ms: 120000
- buffering:
  socket_buffer_mb: 64
  local_queue_mb: 1024
- fallback:
  s3_bucket: "s3://acme-telemetry-archive/forwarder-failures/"
  manifest_fields: ["batch_id","start_ts","end_ts","file_count","sha256s"]

4) OTEL/Tracing hooks
- Deploy an OTEL collector sidecar in the same pod. Configure a transform to add attributes: {"redwood_request_id": "%{redwood.request_id}", "env": "%{env}"}. Export spans to our tracing gateway via OTLP/gRPC over port 4317. We'll map trace_id->Splunk field when we index spans.

5) Evidence for audits
- The manifest.json pattern Rishi suggested will be generated automatically for each archived bundle. We'll sign the manifest with a rotating key and include the public certificate in the archive for verification. Naomi will coordinate the artifact format with your auditors.

6) Canary plan
- Day 0: test HEC endpoint with low-volume events (1-5 eps).
- Day 1: 1% production traffic mirrored (no ingestion).
- Day 2-3: incremental ramp with health checks and alerting on error-rate and lag.

Action: Aaron — please provide test HEC host/IP and preferred auth. We can create a test forwarder image and share a deployment manifest for you to run in staging.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
